- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.3) — reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to sentiment peak.
- Underestimate prices after sharp downward spikes — adjust forecast upward by 3–8% if sentiment remains neutral or mildly negative.
- Lagged price drops are often overcorrected — delay forecast correction by 1–2 days if sentiment shows early bearish signals.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- Overshoot after spikes: if forecast exceeds true outcome by >5% for 3+ consecutive days, apply downward pressure of 1–2% per day.
- Sentiment reversal triggers: if sentiment drops below 0.15 after peak, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence — cap forecast at 10% below 30-day moving average if sentiment is weak or volatile.
